sections.h2: How can you sell a house fast in Irvington, New Jersey?
sections.html:
Irvington owners can list the house, sell it themselves or accept a cash offer for the property as-is, and in every case the township requires a housing inspection before the title transfers. That rule shapes the timeline more than any other local factor, so start it as soon as you decide to sell.

The township has a high share of renters and small multi-family buildings, so many sellers are landlords or heirs rather than owner-occupants. Two-family and three-family houses are common, and the fee and paperwork scale with the number of units.

  • Listing: best for a house that will pass inspection with little work and appraise well.
  • Private sale: works if you can manage the inspection, the contract and the buyer's financing without an agent.
  • Cash sale: fits a house with code violations, tenants or probate complications, because the purchase contract can be written around the condition.

sections.h2: Where is Irvington and how did it get its name?
sections.html:
Irvington is a small, dense township of 2.92 square miles in Essex County. Maplewood lies to the west and Newark to the east, with Hillside and Union to the south and southwest. The Elizabeth River runs through it near Civic Square.

Until the middle of the 1800s the place was called Camptown. After a well-known ballad about Camptown races was published in 1850, residents worried about the association and renamed it for the author Washington Irving. It became an incorporated village on March 27, 1874, a town in 1898, and a township after a 1982 referendum.

An amusement park, Olympic Park, straddled the Irvington and Maplewood line from 1887 to 1965. Population rose from 1,677 in 1880 to about 61,000 in 1980 and has stayed near that level ever since: 61,176 in the 2020 census, and 62,233 in the July 2025 estimate.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Irvington housing and residents?
sections.html:
Irvington is a rental-heavy township with the lowest home values of the four municipalities in the same Census comparison. Only 29.6 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, and the median owned home is worth $335,600, based on 2020 to 2024 estimates in QuickFacts.

Median gross rent is $1,386. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $2,489 a month, and those without pay $1,026. The township has 23,542 households averaging 2.57 people and a median household income of $61,609, while 19.0 percent of residents live in poverty.

About 35.5 percent of residents were born outside the United States, and 32.4 percent of people age 5 and older speak a language other than English at home. That mix is worth keeping in mind when you arrange showings, notices and closing documents; a translated summary of key dates helps family sellers who share ownership.

sections.h2: What does the Certificate of Housing Compliance require when you sell in Irvington?
sections.html:
Irvington's code makes it unlawful to sell, convey or transfer a building with residential units, or for a buyer to take title or possession, until a Certificate of Housing Compliance has been issued. The Department of Housing issues it after an application and an inspection. The online portal at irvingtonportal.us handles the application and the separate Fire Department inspection.

Irvington certificates and fees, from the Township Code property maintenance chapter on ecode360
CertificateWhen it appliesFee or term
Certificate of Housing ComplianceSale or transfer of a building with residential units$237 per unit up to three units, $116 per unit beyond three
Temporary certificateViolations that will not be fixed before closingNonrenewable, up to six months
Certificate of HabitabilityRenting a dwelling unit to a new tenant$98 per unit, $47 per reinspection, renewed every two years

For an as-is sale, the contract must be attached to the application and signed by both seller and buyer. If the inspection finds violations that stay unrepaired, the director may issue the temporary certificate, and the buyer then acknowledges the duty to fix them. Liability for skipping the certificate falls on both the owner and the purchaser.

The code's exemption section lists transfers between immediate family members, a property inspected within the prior six months, a purchase made to demolish the building and probate transfers to heirs under a will. Ask the Housing Department how those exemptions apply to your sale. A denied certificate can be appealed in writing to the Business Administrator, who must decide within five business days.

sections.h2: Where do you apply, and who inspects?
sections.html:
The Housing and Building office sits in the Municipal Building, Room 201, at 1 Civic Square. Its page lists an evening housing inspector available Monday to Friday from 5:00 to 9:00 p.m. and Saturday from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., which helps working owners schedule around a job.

  • Owners of any building in the township, residential or commercial, must give the Housing Department, Tax Collector and Tax Assessor their true home address and company address.
  • Vacant properties go through the Vacant Property Registration Program, with registration on the township portal.
  • Violation notices become orders if no written petition for a hearing is filed within 10 days, so respond to any notice quickly.
  • Fines under the property maintenance code run from $50 for a first violation to $1,000 for a fourth, which also requires a court appearance.

Irvington's 2.91 square miles of land hold 69.44 miles of road, of which the township maintains 55.98.

sections.h2: How do roads, buses and schools shape the Irvington housing market?
sections.html:
Irvington sits between Newark and the suburbs, and transit is a selling point. The Garden State Parkway passes through the center of the township with exits 143 and 144. Interstate 78 touches the southeastern edge at Exit 54, and County Road 509 is the main local road.

  • Buses: the Irvington Bus Terminal on Springfield Avenue is one of NJ Transit's busiest. Route 107 reaches the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown, and nine routes run to Newark.
  • Air: Newark Liberty International Airport is in neighboring Newark and Elizabeth.
  • Schools: Irvington Public Schools run pre-kindergarten through grade 12 and are one of 31 former Abbott districts. The district had 12 schools and 8,020 students in 2019-20.
  • Business incentives: parts of the township lie in an Urban Enterprise Zone established in May 1996, which expires in May 2027 and allows a reduced 3.3125 percent sales tax at eligible merchants. The area around the bus terminal became a state-designated transit village in July 2015.

sections.h2: What do taxes, recording and state fees add to an Irvington sale?
sections.html:
The Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages records deeds for all 22 municipalities in the county and keeps a copy of every deed and mortgage since 1637. Tax appeals go to the Essex County Board of Taxation, normally by April 1 on Form A-1, with a further appeal to the Tax Court within 45 days of the board's judgment.

The seller pays the State Realty Transfer Fee. At Irvington's median value, the schedule for sales of $350,000 or less applies: $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, $3.35 from $150,000 to $200,000 and $3.90 from $200,000 to $350,000. An owner who lives outside New Jersey, which is common for investor-owned two-families, files GIT/REP-1 and pays an estimated income tax of 2 percent of the price or 8.97 percent of the net gain, unless a stated exemption applies.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate to sell my house in Irvington?
faqs.a: Yes. The Township Code requires a Certificate of Housing Compliance before any building with residential units is sold, conveyed or transferred. The Housing Department issues it after an application and an inspection, and a Fire Department inspection is also part of the process, which can be started on the township's online portal.

faqs.q: How much does the Irvington sale inspection cost?
faqs.a: The code sets $237 per dwelling unit up to three units in a building and $116 for each unit above three. A single-family house therefore costs $237 and a three-family $711. Reinspections carry their own fee, so fix the listed items before the first visit and confirm current amounts with the Housing Department.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Irvington house as-is if it has violations?
faqs.a: Yes, with conditions. The as-is contract must be attached to the application and signed by both parties. If violations remain unrepaired at closing, the director may issue a nonrenewable temporary certificate lasting up to six months, and the buyer acknowledges in writing the duty to bring the property into compliance.

faqs.q: Are any Irvington transfers exempt from the certificate?
faqs.a: The code's exemption section lists family transfers, a property inspected within six months before the transfer, a purchase for demolition and probate transfers to heirs under a will. The wording is older than the latest amendments, so ask the Housing Department to confirm in writing that an exemption covers your sale.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded for an Irvington sale?
faqs.a: At the Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages, which records property transactions for all 22 municipalities in the county. Your title company or closing attorney usually submits the deed with the Realty Transfer Fee affidavit and the GIT/REP form, so you rarely visit the office yourself.
